headline: Two NHL players placed on waivers for Nov. 7
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Atro Leppanen and James Reimer were officially placed on waivers on Saturday. New York Post reporter Mollie Walker posted earlier in the week that Reimer would still back up Dylan Garand that night, calling the move "next step in Joonas Korpisalo's impending return."

Our numbers say the Rangers aren't giving up much. Reimer has played one game so far this season, stopping .625 of the shots he faced. By goals saved above expected, which measures how many goals a goalie stopped compared with what an average goalie would have allowed on the same shots, he sits at -1.96. That is a tiny sample, but it echoes last year: in 14 games he finished at -1.67, so he has now cost his team goals relative to the chances he faced in both stretches. A backup who gives back close to two goals in a single start is a real risk when the starter needs a night off, and the waiver move suggests the Rangers see it the same way. For fantasy, Reimer holds no value, and the one number worth watching is how New York's goaltending looks once Korpisalo is back and the backup job is settled.
